title: Endpoint multiplicity equals incidence count
statement: Let $m$ be a multiset of unordered pairs (edges) drawn from a type $\alpha$, and fix an element $v \in \alpha$. For each edge $e$, let $\{e\}_\ast$ denote the finite set of its endpoints — a singleton when $e$ is a loop and a two-element set otherwise — and form the multiset obtained by concatenating $\{e\}_\ast$ over all $e$ in $m$, counting multiplicities of $m$. Then the multiplicity of $v$ in this concatenated multiset equals the number of edges $e$ of $m$ for which $v$ is an endpoint of $e$.
hypotheses_covered: m is a multiset of unordered pairs (Sym2) over a type with decidable equality
v is a fixed element of the underlying type
replaced:
For a multiset $m$ of unordered pairs and a vertex $v$, the multiplicity of $v$ in the
multiset obtained by binding each edge to its set of endpoints equals the number of
edges of $m$ containing $v$.
